$comment: P0-8 registry. Every top-level collection in firestore.rules MUST have a row here or gate (i) fails. status: ACTIVE (real denial + allow assertions) | PENDING-TENANCY (skipped loudly). Paths use {id}, substituted with the SEEDED tenant-B id named by readDocId/writeDocId - never a random path, because a read of a missing document is denied for the wrong reason. sameTenant: 'allow' means the probe seeds allowDocId for tenant A and the suite asserts tenant A CAN read it (the control that stops a rules typo that denies everything from scoring green); 'none' means no tenant-scoped principal can read that collection and sameTenantWhy must say why.

admins.why: D-038 (card 7): the roster is tenant state. The row uses the owner principal (a customer token is denied by role, which would prove nothing about tenant scope) and asserts that owner A is denied tenant B's rows while still reading its own.

analyticsEvents.sameTenantWhy: Read is owner/manager only; the suite has no admin principal for tenant A.
analyticsEvents.why: ACTIVE: analytics read/writes are tenant-scoped. No allow control: read is owner/manager only, and the suite has no admin principal.

audit_log.why: D-038 (card 7): the audit log is tenant state, readable by the owner only. Probed with the owner principal: tenant A's owner reads its own entries and is denied tenant B's; writes are denied to everyone (Admin SDK only).

audit_logs.why: D-038 (card 7): same contract as audit_log — owner-readable within the tenant, never writable from a client.

branches.sameTenantWhy: Public branch read survives tenancy: a guest of the same tenant still needs it to open the app.
branches.why: ACTIVE: a branch is read only inside the caller's tenant (guest boot included) and written by the tenant owner; tenant A still reads its own branch.

branches/config.sameTenantWhy: Operating hours are read on checkout by every app-verified user of the tenant.
branches/config.why: ACTIVE: operating hours are tenant-scoped on read and owner-written inside the tenant.

branches/menu_overrides.sameTenantWhy: The public menu-override overlay survives tenancy: a guest of the same tenant still needs it to render the menu.
branches/menu_overrides.why: ACTIVE: the overlay read and its manager write are tenant-scoped; tenant A still reads its own override.

branches/waitlist_meta.sameTenantWhy: Every app-verified guest reads the ordinal doc to compute a position; tenant A reads its own.
branches/waitlist_meta.why: ACTIVE: the ordinal doc is tenant-scoped on read and on the join/serve transaction writes.

carts.sameTenantWhy: carts/{uid} is self-read; tenant A reads its own cart by uid.
carts.why: ACTIVE: a cart is self-keyed and tenant-scoped; tenant A reads its own cart.

deletion_requests.sameTenantWhy: deletion_requests/{uid} is self-read; tenant A reads its own erasure marker.
deletion_requests.why: ACTIVE: an erasure marker is self-keyed and tenant-scoped.

deliveries.why: D-047 (card 8): the delivery document cannot carry a tenantId — the driver GPS ping is hasOnly-shaped and replaces the document — so the rule scopes it through the ORDER it belongs to (the same document it already reads for assignedDriverId). Reads are asserted with the owner principal; the write denial happens by ROLE first, which is stated here rather than counted as tenant proof.

driverLocations.sameTenantWhy: driverLocations/{driverId} is self-read for the driver; tenant A reads its own location doc.
driverLocations.why: ACTIVE: a driver location is self-keyed (driverId == uid) and tenant-scoped.

locations.sameTenantWhy: locations is app-verified read for any signed-in user.
locations.why: ACTIVE: locations read and writes are tenant-scoped; tenant A reads its own location doc.

loyalty.why: ACTIVE: a loyalty ledger is self-keyed and tenant-scoped.

menus.sameTenantWhy: The guest-boot menu read is the path design 1 puts at risk; this is the primary positive control.
menus.why: ACTIVE: menus read is tenantOk() and the probe seeds both tenants at registry ids, so a leak and a lockdown both fail.

notification_queue.sameTenantWhy: Owner/manager only; no tenant-scoped principal for tenant A in the suite.
notification_queue.why: ACTIVE: owner/manager readability and owner writes, tenant-scoped. No allow control by design (queue writes are owner-only).

notifications.why: ACTIVE: a mailbox is self-keyed and tenant-scoped; its items subcollection carries the same clauses.

notifications/items.sameTenantWhy: A mailbox item is self-read by the mailbox owner, and the parent is that same uid.
notifications/items.why: ACTIVE: a mailbox item is tenant-scoped and self-keyed; tenant A still reads its own item.

orders.sameTenantWhy: An order is readable by its own customer (customerId == uid).
orders.why: ACTIVE: order read, create and update are tenant-scoped. The create case is two-sided (D-039): a tenant-A create must succeed and the same body stamped with tenant B must be denied.

presence.sameTenantWhy: Staff read only (owner, or manager/kitchen/delivery scoped to a branch).
presence.why: ACTIVE: presence is staff-only and tenant-scoped. No allow control: a customer cannot read presence.

promoCodes.sameTenantWhy: Read is owner/manager only by design (customers validate through the callable).
promoCodes.why: ACTIVE: owner/manager readability and owner writes, tenant-scoped. No allow control by design (no tenant-scoped readable principal below owner/manager).

promo_usage.why: ACTIVE: promo usage is self-read by userId and tenant-scoped.

promotions.why: ACTIVE: promotions read is tenantOk() and the probe seeds both tenants; tenant A still reads its own banner.

proof_of_delivery.why: D-047 (card 8): proof is scoped through the order named in its orderId field. Owner reads carry the tenant-scoped assertions; writes are driver-only, so the write denial is by role before tenancy is consulted.

reservation_counters.sameTenantWhy: Booking counters are read inside the reservation transaction by any app-verified user.
reservation_counters.why: ACTIVE: a counter is readable to the tenant and tenant-scoped on read, create and update; delete stays denied outright.

reservation_locks.sameTenantWhy: A lock is readable by the user who holds it.
reservation_locks.why: ACTIVE: a lock is readable by its holder and tenant-scoped.

reservations.sameTenantWhy: A reservation is readable by the user who made it (userId == uid).
reservations.why: ACTIVE: reservation read, create, update and delete are tenant-scoped. The create case is two-sided (D-039): a tenant-A booking must succeed and the same body stamped tenant B must be denied.

settings.why: D-038 (card 7): settings documents are keyed by tenant and name (tenantId_name), so the rule can require the document id to start with the caller tenant. The three literal rows the 5a parser registered (restaurantConfig, taxRates, defaultOperatingHours) are gone: those blocks no longer exist separately, this one block covers them.

transactions.sameTenantWhy: The ledger is owner-only read and server-only write; a tenant-scoped tenant A principal cannot read it.
transactions.why: ACTIVE: the ledger read is owner-only AND tenant-scoped. No allow control: no tenant-scoped principal can read it.

users.why: ACTIVE: a user document is readable by its owner and tenant-scoped; tenant A reads its own profile.

waitlist.sameTenantWhy: A waitlist entry is readable by the user queued (userId == uid).
waitlist.why: ACTIVE: a waitlist entry is readable by the queued user and tenant-scoped.

waitlist_counters.sameTenantWhy: Waitlist counters are read inside joinWaitlist by any app-verified user.
waitlist_counters.why: ACTIVE: a counter is readable to the tenant and tenant-scoped on read, create and update; delete stays denied outright.
